title: Brand-primary token conflict — #003366 vs #0373DF
observed: The design library, the Handoff frames and the live portal all use navy #003366 as the brand primary, but the workspace token documentation lists gov-blue #0373DF. Until one is chosen, every primary surface across the portals is ambiguous.
recommendation: Adopt #003366 as the single canonical Primary (it matches the design library, the Handoff file and the live build) and update the token documentation and @mosje/tokens. If #0373DF is actually intended, reverse the decision — but pick one now.

title: Neutral grey ramp is missing from the design system
observed: The library defines only Neutral #374151 plus white. The build needs greys for muted text, borders and surfaces, so developers reached for un-governed values (#4b5563, #6b7280, #9ca3af, #1f2937, #e2e8f0, #f8fafc) on every screen.
recommendation: Add a tokenised neutral ramp (Neutral 50–900) to the design system and Figma variables so the build can map every grey to a token.

title: Missing brand tokens: gov-yellow & active-nav surface
observed: #FFD323 (the BETA badge yellow) and #E5EFF9 (the sidebar active-item surface used consistently on every screen) are not tokens in the library.
recommendation: Add Accent/Gov-Yellow #FFD323 and Surface/Nav-Active #E5EFF9 (or derive it from Primary/100) so these consistent usages are governed.

title: Define a radius scale
observed: The library defines a single radius token (button-corner 8). The build and the designs use 4, 6, 8, 12 and 14px corners in different places.
recommendation: Publish an explicit radius scale (e.g. xs 4 / sm 8 / md 12 / lg 14) so component corners are intentional and consistent on both sides.

title: Masthead headline: 'Department' vs 'Ministry'
observed: The Figma masthead reads 'Department of Social Justice & Empowerment' as the bold headline; the live portal reads 'Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment'. One of them is the wrong entity name — the dev report asks the build to match the design, but the design itself should be confirmed first.
recommendation: Confirm the correct entity name with stakeholders and update the Figma masthead accordingly, so design and build can converge on the right name.

title: Sidebar navigation in Figma is a generic template
observed: Several design frames show a generic multi-scheme MoSJE navigation, while the live eUtthan portal has its own specific menu (Manage Financial Year / Ministry / Scheme / Outcome / Documents, Map Ministry/Schemes, User & Role Management, PFMS Logs, Reports).
recommendation: Update the Figma sidebar to the actual eUtthan navigation so the design file reflects the shipped product (or confirm the generic nav is intentional shell scaffolding).

title: Design an empty state for data tables
observed: When a table has no rows, the build shows a bare 'No Data Found' line. No empty state exists in the design file, so the build improvised.
recommendation: Design a reusable table empty-state (illustration or icon, short message, and the primary action e.g. '+ Add Scheme') and add it to the design system.

title: Role Management — built, never designed
observed: The screen exists live (role list with permissions) but has no Figma frame.
recommendation: Create the Figma frame using the eUtthan visual language (navy #003366, Noto Sans, the standard table card and toolbar patterns).

title: PFMS Logs — built, never designed
observed: The PFMS Logs screen exists live but has no Figma frame.
recommendation: Create the Figma frame following the standard list/table pattern; include the log-status chips in DS colours.

title: Reports · Financial Summary — built, never designed
observed: The Financial Summary report exists live but has no Figma frame.
recommendation: Create the Figma frame (filters row + summary table) using the DS table and chip components.

title: Reports · Statement 10A — built, never designed
observed: The Statement 10A report exists live but has no Figma frame.
recommendation: Create the Figma frame using the DS report-table pattern, consistent with the Financial Summary proposal.
